title: Who, How, and What of Encouragement

body: Some crucial questions regarding loving encouragement are worth answering.

I challenge you to recall the last time you deliberately gave encouragement to your mate. Because of an understanding of his or her fear, you stepped in and extended a statement of strength. And how about your children? Or a very close friend? Let’s not assume others don’t need it, even though they don’t drop hints.
That explains why it has to be a close relationship. You don’t walk up to a stranger and say those words. You say them to only those with whom a deep level of love and acceptance has been cultivated.

Remember the primary principle: Words that encourage are inspired by love and directed toward fear. No doubt about it, we need to know what we believe and why we believe it. A church stands firmer amidst stormy times when its members are doctrinally sound. But no amount of doctrine will replace our need for encouraging relationship built on love and understanding. Knowledge may strengthen, but relationships soften. A healthy church family has both.

author: Charles R. Swindoll
